structure.title: Recruiting an audience
structure.text: Richard introduces his plans and draws others into them through tailored performances of loyalty, grievance, and modesty.

structure.title: Managing the consequences
structure.text: Public display and private coercion work together as his ambitions alter the choices available to allies and opponents.

people.name: The royal family
people.text: Relatives whose claims and fears complicate succession.

context.title: A disputed succession
context.text: Family relationships carry claims to rule. Deaths, marriages, and children therefore become matters of national power.

context.title: History as drama
context.text: Shakespeare's Richard is a dramatic construction within a partisan historical tradition, not a neutral biography of the historical king.
context.takeaway: Separate theatrical character from historical verdict.

notice.why: Enjoying Richard's wit can create uncomfortable complicity.
Political consent can be carefully staged.

opening: Richard tells the audience what he intends to do, then walks into the next room and tells everyone else what they need to hear. He can flatter, mourn, threaten, and pretend reluctance with astonishing speed. Watching him work is pleasurable enough to make the pleasure uncomfortable: his wit invites us into plans whose victims have no such privileged view. Shakespeare follows the making of a king through a society full of people willing to accommodate one more outrage, provided it appears to serve their interests.
